**Short answer: R3 looks like a theorem, not a conjecture, wherever the equation space is generated by equations of at most three distinctions.** I have not opened the repo definitions; this assumes a bond is a minimal-support vector of the equation space (over GF(2)) and a symmetry is a permutation of distinctions.

**(3) Proof route**
1. A triple has reading 2 (three, less one) exactly when the triple itself is a bond, since a bond of size 3 holding S is S. Likewise a pair has distance 1 exactly when it is a 2-bond.
2. So a symmetry keeping pair and three-way readings maps every bond of size ≤ 3 to a bond of size ≤ 3.
3. Every vector of a binary space is a disjoint union of minimal-support vectors. So each generating equation with ≤ 3 distinctions splits into bonds of size ≤ 3, and those bonds span the equation space.
4. The symmetry is an injective linear map sending a spanning set of the space into the space, so by dimension it carries the space onto itself.

There are two gaps to check:
- **Size-1 bonds:** a fixed distinction must be visible in the table. I think it is, as "none" against every other distinction, but confirm.
- **Generators:** every reached stage's equation space must really be generated by rows of ≤ 3 places. Your "sharing up to 4/3" suggests some 4-place junctions; if so, the argument only covers stages where the ≤ 3-bonds still span.

**(1) Plausibility and counterexamples**
- R3 is plausible on that class for the reason above. It also explains why pairs alone fail: pair data sees 2-bonds exactly but 3-bonds only through sizes.
- I know of no named graphic counterexample.
- Outside graphic matroids, sparse paving matroids with many circuit-hyperplanes have constant pair and triple cocircuit data yet differ.
- For graphs, the place to look is 4-regular, 4-edge-connected graphs, where no bond has size ≤ 3 and three-way readings only report sizes. K5 is not one: its pair table is already the line graph, which is rigid.
- The general statement is "k-way readings are rigid when bonds of size ≤ k span."

**(2) Hunt**
- I see no soundness flaw in the multiset-restricted VF2.
- If the lemma holds, most of the hunt replays a theorem. Before freezing, add a cheap discriminator: for each stage, compare the rank of the span of bonds of size ≤ 3 with the rank of the equation space.
- Stages with equal rank are settled by proof. Spend the symmetry enumeration on deficit stages only, since a failure can only live there.
- If there are no deficit stages, record the hunt as a replay of the lemma, not as evidence.

**(4) Bets**

| Claim | If generators have ≤ 3 places | If 4-place generators occur |
|---|---|---|
| R3 holds on the hunt | 97% | 85% |
| R3 true for all reached stages | 95% | 60% |
| R3 true for all connected arrangements | true by the lemma | 20% (I expect a 4-edge-connected counterexample) |
